content:
Nadia: Heads-up: InkWell's onboarding is tripping our per-client rate limits during their server-side warmup. They run many short-lived Lambdas that call our SDK on cold start and we're seeing synchronized retries -> big 429 spikes. Can someone triage?
Ibrahim: classic cold-start stampede. Short-lived containers + SDK default retry behavior (no jitter + high concurrency) will sync retries. Do we have example logs?
Customer-Infra: pasted a short trace:
[2026-12-01T03:10:01Z] lambda coldstart x-client-id: inkwell-svc-1 preflight 200
[2026-12-01T03:10:04Z] lambda coldstart preflight 429 many
[2026-12-01T03:10:10Z] lambda retry preflight 429 backoff
[2026-12-01T03:10:18Z] lambda retry preflight 200
Customer-Infra: they also spawn 10 parallel worker processes on boot which all call init concurrently.
Ibrahim: two parallel tracks: client changes + infra short-term ops. Client: 1) enable full jitter on SDK retries, 2) lower maxRetries for ephemeral warmup calls, 3) memoize token fetch per process, 4) use HTTP/2 or keep-alive pool so warmup doesn't open many new TCP/TLS connections. Example Node hint: `sdk.config({ retries: 2, jitter: 'full' })`.
SDK-Bot: Note: Node SDK v2.6 has a helper `coalesceEphemeral()` that will return the same inflight promise across calls. We can ship a tiny patch to enable it by default for serverless runtimes.
Nadia: if we ship a patch can we fast-track it? Customer is concerned about renewal impact if production is shaky.
Ibrahim: infra short-term: offer a 12h soft warmup bump and tag their x-client-id so edge can apply relaxed shaping. Also suggest they stagger deployment across regions to avoid global burst.
EdgeOps: agree to a 12h bump. @OnboardBot create ticket LAMBDA-ONB-03, owner EdgeOps, ETA 45m.
OnboardBot: Created ticket #LAMBDA-ONB-03 for temporary warmup capacity (12h), owner: EdgeOps, ETA: 45m.
Customer-Infra: quick client-side change they applied:
```js
// reduce retries + enable jitter
sdk.config({ maxRetries: 1, retryDelayMs: 300, jitter: 'full' });
// coalesce token fetch per process
let ep=null; async function getTok(){ if(ep) return ep; ep = fetch('/auth/ephemeral').finally(()=> setTimeout(()=> ep=null, 60000)); return ep; }
```
Customer-Infra: after those patches 429s dropped from ~400/min to ~25/min during the next cold-start window.
Ibrahim: nice. Follow-up asks: 1) mark their client id `inkwell-svc-1` in our onboarding list so we can relax IP shaping, 2) run a small canary with 5% traffic before full rollout, 3) we should offer the small SDK patch to coalesce by default for serverless environments.
EdgeOps: added `inkwell-svc-1` to relaxed shaping list and will monitor for 2h.
Nadia: CS handoff checklist to send customer: ["enable SDK full jitter","lower maxRetries for warmup calls","coalesce ephemeral token in process","enable HTTP keep-alive/HTTP2 if possible","ops temp bump ticket LAMBDA-ONB-03","canary 5% rollout then monitor 2h"]. I'll message them and offer the SDK patch.
Customer-Infra: thanks team, deploying the canary now and will report back in 30m.
SDK-Bot: I can open a PR for the opt-in serverless coalescing helper, tag `sdk-pr/inkwell-coalesce`.
Nadia: perfect. Closing thread after canary stable and 2h monitoring. :white_check_mark:
